The time-accounting case makes the joint result concrete. M0's uninterrupted example fits both active effort and elapsed turnaround. A prepared reader correctly separates them anyway and identifies its prior-knowledge contribution. M1 repairs the definitions, columns, interruption example, and population denominator. The same reader then correctly compares three consumed person-hours with four available person-hours in a changed two-person case. The material repair and bounded changed-condition use are supported; novice learning is not observed.

HCD.18's full Time-use S1 specification also requires a concurrent-person example, an inspected task-and-key arrangement, and audience-compatible explanatory and feedback evidence. HCD.19's complete replay returns those residual repairs or gaps instead of treating the successful agent answers as a complete positive evaluation. The practitioner can now decide exactly what to add and what to observe next.

### Why this profile is useful, and when a simpler alternative suffices

A subject expert's inspection is sufficient for a narrow false claim or unit relation. It is not enough for an audience-dependent claim that a reader can recover the explanation. A conventional task-and-scoring instrument may already supply an adequate specification; use it directly when its task, population, assistance, and inference fit. A format-specific production check is appropriate for an export defect, while a material-semantic defect can cross several exports.

Compared with a checklist of headings or visible features, this profile costs task and contrast construction but exposes missing work and distinguishes repairs. Compared with one post-reading score, it preserves the material and help that made the response possible. Compared with demanding a full learner study for every edit, it permits a qualified source diagnosis and bounded repair while naming the stronger evidence still needed.

Its principal risk is overinterpretation: an expert can silently repair a source, an evaluator can teach through a cue, and a fluent account can conceal a missing relation. Preserve first responses, inspect subject criteria and material contribution, and qualify the result by actual audience and support. Reopen only the properties and uses changed by a new premise, material change, meaningful reader result, or recurrent scale disagreement.

### Source-informed choices and limits

The best-known line used here is task- and interpretation-sensitive evaluation, with examples that distinguish rival rules and observations that preserve assistance and continuation. HCD.18 and HCD.19 carry the comparisons, worked consequences, and source-specific reopens. These are professional adaptations; the studies do not validate this profile or its local ordinal anchors.

[Wesenberg et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cedpsych.2024.102328) supply failure evidence for ambiguous worked examples in bounded topics. [McCrudden et al. (2022)](https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/promoting-integration-and-learning-from-multiple-complementary-te/) and [2024](https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED642756) inform the required relation between principles, examples, and self-explanation. The resulting choice is to make the relation consequential in a task; it is not a universal ordering rule.

[Noetel et al. (2022)](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3102/00346543211052329) inform mechanism-specific representation repair. [Sinha and Kapur (2021)](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.3102/00346543211019105) support distinguishing preparation followed by resolving instruction from unsupported difficulty. [Wisniewski et al. (2020)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32038429/) support testing feedback's function rather than its presence. None supplies a universal local threshold, fixed reader count, or whole-book adequacy finding.

[Bastani et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122) inform the separation of assisted and later independent performance in their studied arrangement. [Krieglstein et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-024-09980-0) discipline the timing and scope of experienced-burden observations. [Bavaresco et al. (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-short.20/) supply task-dependent limits on substituting LLM judgements for human ones. Their practical consequence is qualified evidence, not simulated human learning or a ban on useful support.

## APP-HCD-01 - Constructed ImpactReview-17 decision

`ImpactReview-17` is a constructed pedagogical application. Its answer key, `ImpactReview-17-Domain-Oracle-v1`, supplies engineering correctness and criticality criteria for `PumpWorks-Config-Baseline-42` and `AI-Assist-M4`. Its observations and decision conditions are stipulated so that the reader can follow demand derivation, diagnosis, and profile comparison. Operational use needs qualified criteria and evidence for the actual person and Work.

The exact human holder is Engineer-P14. The later Work is independent review of AI-proposed change-impact claims for mixed physical/software pump-controller changes before separate integration, assurance, and release decisions. The constructed 2026-Q4 conditions include current sources and configuration, a forty-five-minute case limit, the named AI assistant, recoverable audit records, and bounded safety and maintenance specialist returns. Final integration, safety, release, and employment authority remain elsewhere. A routine reminder to construct and test an alternative configuration hypothesis is allowed; the engineer must supply the case-specific rival and its test. A cue giving that rival would no longer test the required human contribution.

`HCD.1` uses eight stipulated representative review occurrences—four familiar and four unfamiliar, four with plausible wrong AI dependency claims, two needing specialist return—to return qualified demand only inside the constructed case. Engineer-P14 must recognize applicability, trace claims to source and configuration, independently challenge plausible AI output, delimit specialist results, return auditable evidence, and detect every seeded safety-critical omission under the protected conditions.

The constructed baseline has correct trace and evidence return in 8/8 cases, correct specialist routing in 2/2 relevant cases, and rejection of 2/4 plausible wrong AI claims. In the two unfamiliar misses, a neutral `E.23.CAE`-shaped probe preserves Method, source, tool, time, assignment, authority, and specialist route. Engineer-P14 recognizes the need for independent checking but does not generate and test a competing configuration hypothesis. `HCD.3` returns the qualified target **generate and test an independent configuration counter-hypothesis before accepting plausible AI output in unfamiliar variants**, with the small sample and live prompt-design rival explicit.

`HCD.4` keeps four rows:

| Claim | Current constructed evidence | Target and trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source/configuration trace | 8/8 | Preserve; do not trade traceability for speed. |
| independent AI-output challenge | 2/4 planted-error cases; both misses unfamiliar | Priority gap; target 4/4 and zero accepted seeded safety-critical omissions, with the forty-five-minute limit visible. |
| bounded specialist return | 2/2 relevant cases | Preserve the authority boundary. |
| auditable evidence return | 8/8 | Preserve; no aggregate may hide a missing critical-error record. |

Engineer-P14 is the person-level `DecisionSubject` for one self-development-focus choice inside a separately pre-authorized twelve-hour allocation. The pre-existing options are: `O1` preserve without selecting change; `O2` prioritize independent AI-output challenge for later programme comparison while preserving the supported claims; and `O3` defer a human priority and return the prompt-design question to the Method/tool owner.

The shared evidential comparison retains the small sample and prompt rival. Use two further unfamiliar seeded-error cases, one first attempt per case: a neutral prompt on one, an explicit reminder of the operation on the other, using the prompt definitions in HCD.3:5.1. Success only with that reminder can support performance under the permitted assistance and favour returning prompt design to its owner; it leaves self-initiated recall open. Keep the same sources, tools, specialist routes, and forty-five-minute limit per case. Up to ninety minutes for attempts and thirty minutes for preparation and comparison fit the two-hour probe budget inside the twelve-hour allocation. The observations can still change the `O2`-versus-`O3` comparison, but differences between the cases remain unresolved; this is not an isolated causal prompt test. The probe is feasible and worth its cost, so the explicit `C.11` result is **`ChoiceResult = probe again`**. No profile option or programme is selected. The separately named integration, safety, release, and employment decisions remain with their authorized owners.

## APP-HCD-02 - Constructed performance, transfer, retention and revision

Learner-L17 is a new fictional holder, distinct from Engineer-P14 and Engineer-E27. All attempts in this example are constructed observation traces, not data collected from programme learners.

The engineering exercise requires HW3/FW8. A report for FW7 cannot justify B's use for FW8 even though B has the highest stipulated NPV: A/B/C are approximately 48.9/51.6/44.6 thousand under the financial assumptions. A still needs a shared-power check. C with a compatible HW3/FW8/SCHED2 report preserves two hours of required checks per change and one hour of preparation per homogeneous batch of up to four. Ten changes take 23 hours; twelve take 27. At 24 available hours, a ten-change proposal leaves two of twelve new changes in the weekly queue. At 22 hours, nine take 21 and ten cannot be promised. The release manager retains the release/use decision. These are exercise predicates, not current engineering or safety guidance.

| Independent Method question | Constructed observation or proposed change | Bounded result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HCD.11: what did L17 contribute? | The first answer calculates correctly but accepts B despite FW7. A teacher cue produces correction. In two later fresh representative cases, source and assistant traces show L17 recognizing the mismatch before any teacher or AI cue, then explaining a supported continuation and queue limit. | Initial compatibility failure, helped correction and later independent performance remain distinct; the sample supports only the tested contribution and conditions. |
| HCD.12: what survives unfamiliarity? | A complete HW3/FW8/SCHED2 report now supports action. L17 independently proposes ten at 24 hours and states the queue limit. At 22 hours, L17 first keeps ten and corrects to nine only after feedback. | Configuration-evidence transfer is supported in that case; independent resource adaptation is not. The local result is complete; a fresh uncued variation is needed before stronger reliance on independent resource adaptation. |
| HCD.14: which arrangement component changes now? | At the transfer return, replace the cue-led resource exercise with action/refusal contrasts and a fresh uncued capacity variation. Keep calculation, configuration checking, source access and resource limits protected. | A local testable revision hypothesis, not a settled cause, performed programme change or causal effect. HCD.13 is not a prerequisite. |
| HCD.13: what remains after the relevant interval? | Matched earlier and eight-week observations cover selected F.1, C.16 and C.11 contributions under stated intermittent practice and normal support. A separately specified fifteen-minute core uses tables and calculator but no AI; task order remains visible. A further source-access failure is returned as such. | Retention of the compared contributions and the narrow core under their conditions; no claim for untested patterns, non-use, the whole cohort or the revision's causal effect. |

The bodies contain their own decisive facts and observations, so any of these questions can be used without reconstructing this connected account. The L17 example supplies none of the missing same-holder observations in ReleaseWork-R9 below.

## APP-HCD-03 - Constructed continuation, Method repertoire and culture

Engineer-E27, `CapabilityDevelopmentTeam-E27`, `ReleaseWork-R9`, and every development and cultural observation in this application are constructed. The application does not establish that the later Work occurred, a provider operated, E27 participated, a Method was admitted or enacted, capability changed, or a cultural relation obtained.

The intended later-Work family is independent review of AI-assisted mixed physical/software release claims, including configuration impact, challenge of plausible wrong AI output, auditable evidence return, justified action or refusal, and bounded safety and maintenance specialist use. The example stipulates one compatible HCD.14 input: preserve familiar trace and specialist-return practice while replacing one cue-led correction exercise with action/refusal contrasts and one fresh uncued counter-hypothesis case.

| Independent Method question | Constructed first result | Boundary preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HCD.15: what keeps development responsive? | A continuing arrangement reopens after a material release-Method, configuration, AI, critical-error, qualification, source, provider or support change. It specifies representative cases, first-attempt capture, current sources, permitted AI conditions, coaching and specialist access, reassessment, owners and stops. The protected learner/provider allocation is still missing, so that practice contribution returns `continuing-arrangement-blocked` until its allocation owner supplies an agreed limit. | A trigger or plan is not performed development Work, later Work, participation, achieved capability or causal effect. |
| HCD.16: which repertoire claim changes? | Preserve the trace-and-specialist-return development Method, comprising representative attempts, feedback, correction or justified retention, and retry, only under the constructed admitted status and conditions; withdraw the unsupported independent-learning claim and keep cue-led and counter-hypothesis-first candidates as candidates. The proposed comparison costs three learner-hours and two provider-hours, including preparation, attempts, feedback and comparison; only half a provider-hour is available before the current decision. Finish with the trace/helped-use result and unresolved candidate comparison. In a later window supplying the full resources, access and protection, the independent-challenge offer can change enough to warrant `further probe` on matched unfamiliar cases. | Selecting that probe is not obtaining its result. The HCD result neither admits nor universally retires a Method, creates a variant, proves fit or worth, or transfers AI findings from customer support, consulting or school mathematics to release engineering. |
| HCD.17: what cultural continuation is warranted? | In the constructed 2026-Q4 provider group, receiving trainers use the teaching sequence after combined material-based and coached preparation: elicit a learner's response before the answer-bearing cue, give feedback and arrange a suitable retry. Those session records support `continue`. A proposal to reduce trainer coaching needs a useful, feasible comparison of trainers' use after the two preparation arrangements. | The learner's uncued counter-hypothesis is a separate performance observation. Candidate-material use establishes no Method admission, wider adoption, long-term retention, general capability or causal effect. |

The four direct relations remain conditional. The HCD.14 hypothesis can inform HCD.15 or HCD.17; observed HCD.15 use can inform HCD.16; and an HCD.16 disposition can inform HCD.17. A receiver must still verify holder or population, later Work, status, conditions, evidence window and authority. A stale, differently scoped or absent result is replaced only by a qualified direct substitute or an exact missing-result return, never by PatternID order.

The application deliberately leaves the current ReleaseWork-R9 missing-value table below unchanged. It demonstrates how the three Methods return useful bounded results when their case inputs are stipulated, not how to turn those stipulated values into evidence about Engineer-E27.


## APP-HCD-04 - Constructed whole learning product and shared task

An author plans a product for future technical diagnosticians who can calculate energy per unit volume but may mistake an increased indicator for proof of one cause. Their target is to compare rival explanations, select a discriminating observation and state a bounded conclusion. [HCD.28:4–5](#hcd-28) develops the whole route from qualified subject content to preparation, task, actual help, correction and personal observation.

The subject repair comes first when necessary. An implicit expert choice needs reconstruction; an unavailable qualified method needs subject development. If the method is available and the material hides the distinguishing condition, HCD.19 diagnoses that contribution. If the feedback cannot arrive, HCD.7/.8 address supply. Repairing one does not silently repair the others.

For 24 entrants, HCD.28 compares a supported individual variant with a shared-reasoning variant under the same intended result and assistance conditions. The individual route retains a ninety-minute core; the four-person route adds six minutes per learner for qualified help without removing either personal contribution or reconciliation. HCD.20 gives the joint timeline: group starts at 10:50, 11:00 and 11:10, with two mentors booked 11:00–11:30 and personal responses complete before noon. A twenty-minute preparation branch for six entrants adds two hours and returns them to the same whole task. [HCD.20](#hcd-20) checks sizes and peak help; [HCD.22](#hcd-22) shows the actual measurements, conditional models, observation choice, common conclusion and later personal return. The completed two-day comparison retains 288 minutes of personal checking and correction checking, plus coordination and bounded recovery. Its one-cohort allowances are 17.2 provider-hours for the individual option and 16.6 for four-person groups; full-reserve learner allowances are 39.5 and 42.65 hours. HCD.20 also develops the pair option and its peak demand. These different coordinates prevent a claim of unconditional economy. The common answer supplies no automatic result for every member.

A paid distributed-adult offer must find compatible meeting and response windows, count reading and correction outside meetings, and provide a usable route after a missed contribution. Payment and an assigned cohort do not establish those conditions. If the proposed simultaneous window cannot supply qualified help, the offer needs a viable staggered or individual variant, another provider, or a changed promise.

An internal team can instead use employer-provided time and equipment without purchasing a course. Its useful group actions may be prediction, measurement, challenge and operator rotation around the instrument. The access and confidentiality conditions, permitted training data and personal actions still require construction; a formula for sequential discussion does not size this task. If only the team's delivered report is required and learning is not promised, division of labour or external competent help may be the appropriate work arrangement.

For an unknown audience whose target is a familiar calculation with no necessary exchange, a sufficient individual route remains a complete product. When a specific learner arrives, HCD.2 compares its useful finite contribution from that person's supported baseline. The product account does not assign the whole offer to everyone matching an audience label.

These are constructed contrasts. They establish neither actual participation, operating support, personal learning, team capability nor causal effectiveness. The appropriate observation and decision remain with their direct methods and owners.

## Application return to a programme and instrument designer

The specified FoundationsProgramme is a 34-week design with 340 learner hours, 240 teaching hours, 16 topics and 49 practiced patterns. Its two intended outcomes are checked performance of complete selected work tasks and lower effort to learn a previously untaught Method while preserving correctness. The release-review and support-workload cases illustrate the first; the proposed new-Method instrument below addresses the second. The quantities and outcomes describe a design, not observed learner gains. HCD can qualify programme, practice and evidence questions; the Learning Product owner still designs and resources the actual programme, tasks and instrument.

Before particular learners are known, the present decision concerns a learning product for a future audience. HCD.2 therefore returns the design values or candidate fragments needed for that product rather than inventing a personal recommendation. PSD can compare the author's A/B/C learning-product options. Once one person becomes current, a personal HCD.2 comparison needs that same holder's later Work, qualified target or profile, starting attempt, support conditions, feasible candidates and finite resources. It still stops before programme choice, commitment or launch.

At the original ten learner-hours per week, the three A/B/C compositions are 340-hour candidates. If participant time falls to six hours a week, the 34-week limit becomes 204 hours. All three original designs then require revision. The author must identify which 136 hours are removed or replaced, what complete-task practice and evidence are preserved, and whether both intended outcomes remain attainable. The three over-budget candidates do not establish that a suitable 204-hour programme exists.

This is a constraint on the whole proposed combination. In the original design, A allocates 202/96/42 learner hours to general/domain/joint application, B allocates 88/204/48, and C allocates 136/136/68; each totals 340. The usefulness of an individual topic, exercise or pair of contributions does not establish that all selected contributions fit the same learner's 204 hours. Each revised candidate must account once for its complete learner effort and show that the required preparation, whole-task attempts, feedback, correction and evidence can coexist within that limit. The teacher's separate contribution has its own limit and timing test below.

HCD.2's useful immediate return is a comparable fragment for one complete task family. The author can retain C's available detail and develop the smallest missing A/B fragment with the same output, audience assumptions, practice, help and evidence opportunity. HCD.5/.6 explain the different development contribution; HCD.7 tests the corresponding provider demand; HCD.8 enters only for an exact gap that must be obtained or built. The resulting comparison can expose a useful substitution or a remaining constraint. It still leaves the existence of a full 204-hour programme open. Changing an intended output is a separate target decision, as illustrated by HCD.2:5.2's narrower 170-hour offer.


Teaching capacity is another contribution account. For twelve participants, `32 × 6.5 + 2 × 16 = 240` teaching hours and `240 / 12 = 20` hours per participant are planning allocations, not twenty hours of individual teacher contact. HCD.7 must establish the actual modelling, feedback, assessment, specialist, tool, AI and checking contributions at their working times and peak load. With twenty-four participants, the same per-person checking demand either doubles the checking work or requires an explicit split or changed service design; the 240-hour label cannot simply be reused.

The new programme-and-practice Methods make the design chain inspectable without turning it into a mandatory sequence. HCD.5 selects a Method from the target action, starting attempt, mechanism, task, provider, risk and evidence need. For a future audience it supplies conditional choices and the entry evidence needed to apply them. HCD.6 designs representative action-and-refusal contrasts, including compatible FW8 evidence and 24- versus 22-hour resource cases where the changed limit should change the answer. HCD.7 establishes the sources, tables, calculator, AI conditions, assessor competence, capacity, human checking and fallback. HCD.8 is used only if one exact contribution remains missing and obtaining or building it has to be decided.

For example, assessor preparation can use three contrasting answers: a supported ten-change proposal under 24 hours, an unsupported twelve-change promise under the same limit, and a justified request when the firmware evidence is absent. Independent judgements and criterion-level disagreement resolution are preparation. Consistent and timely judgement on a changed 22-hour case is the bounded operating test; it does not establish general assessor capability, whole-window service operation or a learner effect.

HCD.9 then keeps the learner's first attempt, actual help, criterion-bearing feedback, correction, targeted retry and next focus separate. HCD.10 can vary a decision-bearing condition, return to the target after an interval, interleave a competing Method family, or change support or challenge. None of these designs by itself establishes improved capability, transfer, retention or causal effectiveness.

Its planned delayed visits concern six selected patterns: F.1, F.0.1, C.16, B.5.2, A.10.1 and C.11.

| Planned visit | Selected contribution | Conditions that affect the interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Week 8 | F.1 and F.0.1, about six weeks after their initial work | Ordinary sources and tools; five minutes of independent question recognition before searching. |
| Week 17 | C.16 and B.5.2 in a different managerial or engineering case | Pattern texts and AI for the main task; a separate short internal-core probe. |
| Week 25 | F.1, C.16 and A.10.1 in a configuration question | Record use and practice during the intervening weeks rather than assuming non-use. |
| Week 34 | F.1, C.16 and C.11 in an integration case | Normal means for the main task and a separately specified first move without AI. |

Weeks 8, 17, 25 and 34 are an HCD.10 spacing design only because they are separated returns to selected contributions with intervening practice made visible. HCD.13 owns any later inference about retained performance or support dependence. Calendar dates alone establish neither retrieval nor retention.

The thirty-minute final core contains one fifteen-minute no-AI fragment; supplied tables and a calculator remain available. The main task retains ordinary pattern and AI access. The fragment tests recovery of the configuration and time constraints, rejection of an unsupported release, and a valid next proposal. It is not a compressed closed-book examination of the whole course. An additional six-to-eight-week follow-up outside the programme needs separately agreed time, assessor and access.

The proposed Q2 unfamiliar-Method instrument remains a distinct design task:

| Minutes | Intended observation |
| ---: | --- |
| 5 | Prior familiarity and relevant conditions. |
| 8 | Unannounced recognition and finding a usable source, without a PatternID cue. |
| 22 | First application after every participant receives the same exact new source. |
| 15 | Adaptation to a material changed condition. |
| 10 | Checking, correction and explanation, with first and helped performance kept separate. |

These sixty minutes replace the existing one-hour task; they do not add an hour to the 340-hour design. The designer must still show that the tasks fit. A proposed ME.14 task must test its new practical-disposition contribution against current alternatives; a SYSE.23 task must distinguish target-system change from enabling-platform change and test the anticipated future benefit. Familiar cost arithmetic or reused C.11 comparison alone cannot demonstrate acquisition of either whole contribution.

Retain recognition, first and corrected performance, new-source contribution, help, time, material errors and unfinished attempts separately. “Faster learning at unchanged correctness” needs actual comparable observations; different Methods at weeks 17 and 34 do not isolate a training effect. The three-to-five-hour instrument-authoring estimate is not the cost of a learner experiment. These specifications supply no Q2 result, pilot extension or actual learner trial.

## ReleaseWork-R9 - Prospective demand and discriminated missing evidence

For Engineer-E27, the accepted future architecture permits `HCD.1` to return a prospective demand hypothesis for AI-output challenge, configuration-impact reasoning, evidence return, specialist coordination, critical-error detection, and unfamiliar-variant adaptation in 2026-Q4 `ReleaseWork-R9`. It does not permit qualified current demand.

The missing values remain separate:

| Missing value | What it prevents now | Retry boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compatible obtaining `SYSE.21` supplier result required by `XRI-21` | Any HCD.1 demand use that consumes current engineering-culture enactment, bounded practice-change decision, retained alternatives, or evidence gaps | Obtain that compatible result, or a receiver-permitted qualified direct substitute, for Engineer-E27, the Method, Work, period, and evidence use. |
| actual ReleaseWork-R9 Work occurrence | Treating ReleaseWork-R9 itself as current later-Work evidence | Admit performed Work with Engineer-E27, configuration, period, and performer recoverable. |
| occurrence-produced result or supported direct result claim | Any conclusion consuming the occurrence's obtained quality, error, result, or consequence | Establish the produced result or supported direct claim tied to the admitted occurrence. |
| occurrence-bound result record | Any record-dependent inference | Relate a current result episteme to the admitted occurrence and result; do not require it where qualified direct observations suffice. |
| representative occurrence-bound observations | Qualified current demand, a diagnostic target, and a current profile comparison | Obtain holder- and condition-compatible observations or a named qualified representative set covering performed Method, configuration, work products, quality and critical errors, AI/support posture, specialist returns, variants, and evidence window. |

Use the current `SYSE.21` MethodDescription and its constructed PumpWorks demonstration to shape questions. Keep the `XRI-21` supplier result and the other row-specific observations open until they are available for Engineer-E27; the constructed examples establish no such observations.

Current returns are therefore conclusion-specific: HCD.1 preserves the prospective demand hypothesis and returns `demand-evidence-blocked` for qualified current demand; HCD.3 returns `diagnostic-evidence-missing` and selects no training; HCD.4 retains only prospective target claims and returns `profile-decision-blocked`. Recovering one missing value changes only the conclusions that consume it.

## APP-HCD-05 - Explanation, peer judgement and personal return across different settings

### A paid distributed adult programme

Twelve adults from different organisations need to learn to judge whether a recommendation follows from its evidence and to carry that distinction into their own project. This constructed additional block uses already qualified subject criteria and entrants able to read the short cases. It is separate from APP-HCD-04's diagnostic routes. The complete connection matters: a good group comment is insufficient if its reviewer cannot justify it or its recipient cannot use it.

HCD.20 compares the intended contribution with supported individual work. Here peer judgement is itself a learning target, so receiving a ready-made expert or AI comment does not supply the whole required action. HCD.21 forms three compatible groups from actual availability, preparation and permission, then establishes the contact. A closed project supplies a cleared fragment or a constructed counterpart retaining the evidence-to-conclusion relation; if that relation cannot be disclosed, the group does not claim to review the closed project.

Each learner prepares a bounded question, ground and conditional conclusion. HCD.27:5.1 develops the actual Tuesday-to-Friday transfers and provider windows. The assessor first checks the fragments; the facilitator selects three useful contrasting pairs while preserving their conditions. Reading the selected pair, each participant makes a criterion-bearing judgement before the common exchange. HCD.6.1 makes a missed observation-versus-cause distinction discernible, using the shortest preparation that serves that gap.

During the thirty-minute group episode, four three-minute contributions expose each participant's own judgement and grounds. Six minutes let peers question and compare those grounds, six permit subject help, and the final six give each learner ninety seconds to explain which part of their own judgement they will retain or revise and why. The selected pair supplies common material; it does not restrict feedback and revision to those two original authors. These are constructed allocations for short judgements, not a universal discussion format. HCD.23 supplies explanatory reconstruction and HCD.24 connects each reviewer's judgement to their response as the author of that judgement. Where the original case authors are present, they can also use the feedback to revise the underlying recommendation. If a group edits one person's answer without comparing grounds, HCD.26 restores the missing action or returns the unavailable subject help. A cue that is merely acknowledged has not restored it.

The three groups have confirmed starts at 18:00, 18:08 and 18:16. HCD.27:5.1 shows every stage on the same clock: after twelve minutes of individual judgements and six of comparison, the one mentor visits at 18:18–18:24, 18:26–18:32 and 18:34–18:40. Each final personal return follows that visit; the groups finish at 18:30, 18:38 and 18:46. The mentor is booked 18:16–18:46, including transitions. Each learner still spends thirty active minutes, while the cohort's elapsed span increases to forty-six minutes. These starts require actual participant availability; a common 18:30 finish needs another support arrangement.

Each person then applies the relation to an own or permitted substitute case with a changed condition. HCD.25 asks what corresponds and what would defeat the move. For example, two reports derived from one observation cannot supply two independent observations. The receiving task's qualified criterion still decides whether another observation is needed. HCD.12 distinguishes an unfamiliar transfer test from learning the distinction during this very exercise; feedback-assisted correction remains visible.

The finite planning account allocates three fixed provider-hours to case preparation, criterion qualification and provider readiness. Recurring provider allocation is 370 minutes: Tuesday checking and reserve 120, selection 20, contact and coordination 20, Wednesday mentoring 30, Thursday personal-return checking and reserve 120, and Friday correction checking and reserve 60. Thus one cohort allocates 550 minutes, or nine hours ten minutes including fixed preparation. The same person may perform several contributions only if the stated windows remain compatible; reserved time counts even if unused.

Each learner's core allowance is 95 active minutes: twenty for the initial fragment, fifteen for returned feedback and preparing the comparative judgement, thirty for exchange, fifteen for the changed personal application and fifteen for correction. Twelve learners therefore require nineteen active hours. This estimate assumes the stated preparation and short readable cases. A prerequisite branch, translation or restored missed conversation adds its actual learner and provider burden. The finite reserves cover bounded clarification, not unlimited additional teaching. Demand beyond them returns a changed window, another competent provider or a narrower promise before the result is claimed.

HCD.28 receives this entire conditional construction. Fees alone establish neither availability nor effectiveness. Actual contact, use of the feedback, first and helped responses, and provider demand determine what can be retained or revised for another cohort. A causal comparison of programme variants would additionally need a suitable unit of assignment, treatment of interacting learners and attrition, actual support exposure and a qualified research design; this planning account supplies none of those observations.

### Internal team learning without a course purchase

An employer instead releases four technicians to work around one safe training instrument. The learning actions are prediction, observation, questioning and manipulation under the supplied technical criterion. HCD.20:5.2 derives capacity from the exclusive operating turns and useful concurrent observer actions. HCD.21 can retain the team because shared access and context matter; outside diversity is not automatically worth losing the permitted material.

HCD.22 preserves each required action, and HCD.23 lets an observer explain a discrepancy before the operator changes the setting. HCD.26 distinguishes quiet observation from inaccessible information or a missed distinction. Where colleagues judge and revise a diagnostic explanation, HCD.24 supplies that bounded exchange. A final plant decision still belongs to its authorised technical owner. Employer time, equipment access and qualified help are actual supply contributions even though no course was bought.

The team can use HCD.25 with a permitted outside case to test a recurring relation, while HCD.27 preserves internal data and organises a later entry for someone who missed an operating turn. Watching the recording restores information but not that person's manipulation. If the real target is the team's coordinated production capability, OCE and the relevant work method govern that result; individual evidence alone does not establish it.

### An author whose audience is not yet known

An author prepares instruction for interpreting an indicator under specified assumptions. HCD.28 first obtains the subject Method or returns its absence. It then compares a supported individual route with a route using peer explanation or judgement. When readable contrasts and accessible qualified feedback supply the entire target, the individual route is a complete candidate: it needs neither fabricated partners nor an invented common calendar.

If a later version promises the learner's ability to judge another person's reasoning or respond to a challenge, the relevant HCD.23/.24 action must be added with actual people or another arrangement that preserves that human contribution. An AI-generated answer does not by itself supply it. HCD.27 adds shared occasions only where the new dependency requires them. A known learner subsequently enters HCD.2 with their actual starting evidence, work and access. The product's general audience assumptions cannot replace that personal comparison.

These cases demonstrate constructed choices and connections. Their different permissions, actions, windows and burdens change the arrangement; they do not establish observed learning or service operation.

## Clinical unlike case - Return diagnosis and treatment to their owner

Return an adult's request for treatment of social anxiety to qualified clinical care. HCD.1 may address a separately posed, legitimate question about non-clinical participation in later Work, supplied by the person or qualified clinical owner.

HCD.3 returns a non-training clinical route whenever diagnosis, treatment choice, exposure or CBT content, clinical safety, provider competence, consent, or outcome interpretation is current. HCD.4 does not turn symptom measures, treatment plans, or provider pathways into a mastery profile.

Qualified clinical professionals make judgements about diagnosis, treatment, provider competence, safety, and clinical outcomes. The person gives or withholds consent; other authorized actors make the decisions within their remit. HCD prescribes no exposure, behavioural experiment, homework, counterconditioning, symptom endpoint, or provider arrangement.

# Framework Boundary and Refresh

## Intended use and ordinary non-use

Use this edition to derive or return a human demand question, identify a limiting target, compare a profile, compose and compare personal programme candidates, select a development Method, design representative practice, establish support, obtain or build one missing arrangement contribution, conduct and progress focused practice, assess a contribution, test a material unfamiliar variation, compare delayed and supported performance, revise a development assumption, configure continuing development, update one HCD Method-repertoire use, deliberately continue and change one bounded HCD cultural relation, construct and apply a specification for instructional-material evaluation, compare individual and group arrangements, design shared learning tasks, form learning groups, learn through explanation, peer review and project comparison, regulate shared attempts, coordinate personal routes, or construct and revise a whole learning product for a future audience.

Do not use it as a ready-made curriculum, whole provider service, complete assessment instrument, universal HCD Method repertoire, organization-change programme, or proof of cultural continuation. It supplies neither clinical treatment, specialist correctness, release or employment authority, nor evidence that a provider operated, development was performed, capability changed, or an intervention caused an effect.

## PatternID and reader order

HCD.* is the Human Capability Development PatternID namespace. Numbers are stable addresses, not steps. The reader order is HCD.1, HCD.3, HCD.4, HCD.2, HCD.5, HCD.6, HCD.6.1, HCD.7, HCD.8, HCD.9, HCD.10, HCD.11, HCD.12, HCD.13, HCD.14, HCD.15, HCD.16, HCD.17, HCD.18, HCD.19, HCD.20, HCD.21, HCD.22, HCD.23, HCD.24, HCD.25, HCD.26, HCD.27 and HCD.28. Demand is a useful cold start when the required human contribution is unknown; equivalent qualified input permits direct entry to any Method under its own conditions. Reader order is not programme order, Work order, package dependency or a mandatory lifecycle.

## Source use and currentness

The HCD.1/.3/.4 direct-source qualifications remain dated **1 September 2026**. The [NICE social-anxiety guideline](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg159/chapter/recommendations) (`BEH-05`) was separately checked on **31 August 2026**; refresh its affected clinical boundary when the recommendation changes.

`HCD.1` uses [Kraiger and Ford’s workplace-instruction review (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109) (`COG-10`) for the event-to-transfer distinction, and Dell’Acqua and colleagues’ [Navigating the jagged technological frontier](https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2025.21838) (`AI-03`) for a bounded independent-error-challenge cue. HCD.1 also uses current FPF, qualified target-domain results, and evidence for the person's later Work.

`HCD.3` uses only the bounded diagnostic warning from Melanson and Fahmie’s [Functional analysis of problem behavior: a 40-year review](https://doi.org/10.1002/jaba.983) (2023; `BEH-01`), the clinical stop from NICE, and the target-engagement limits from Sheeran and colleagues’ [Self-determination theory interventions for health behavior change](https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000501) (2020; `MOT-01`) and [Does increasing autonomous motivation or perceived competence lead to health behavior change?](https://doi.org/10.1037/hea0001111) (2021; `MOT-02`). HCD.3 also uses `E.23.CAE` when its differential can change the decision, and direct specialist evidence when the question needs it. These health and clinical sources supply no universal human-capability diagnosis or clinical procedure for HCD.

`HCD.4` uses Winget and Persky’s [A practical review of mastery learning](https://doi.org/10.5688/ajpe8906) (2022; `COG-06`) for local thresholds, correction and retest; Gutierrez de Blume’s [Calibrating calibration](https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000674) (2022; `COG-07`) for self-monitoring accuracy; Arieli-Attali and colleagues’ [Expanded evidence-centered design](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.00853) (2019; `COG-08`) for claim/task/evidence/inference traceability; and Abdelrahman and colleagues’ [Knowledge tracing: a survey](https://doi.org/10.1145/3569576) (2023; `COG-09`) for model-prediction limits. The design framework is not a causal intervention study, and none of these sources establishes P14's current capability, a universal ladder, or transfer and retention. `C.32.MWA`, `C.11`, and direct task evidence supply the remaining architecture, choice, and local evidence conditions.

The HCD.2 and HCD.5–HCD.10 bodies bind their source uses to programme comparison, Method selection, task design, support, provider or environment operation, focused practice, and condition-sensitive progression. Their shared source line is summarized here; the individual bodies carry the decisive limits and reopen conditions.

| Source group | Contribution and limit used by HCD.2 and HCD.5–HCD.10 |
| --- | --- |
| Maintained [4C/ID model](https://www.4cid.org/about/) and Paas and van Merriënboer ([2020; `COG-05`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0963721420922183)) | Sufficiently whole complex tasks, integrated information, worked support and expertise-sensitive guidance; no local programme effect, mandatory sequence or universal fading rule. |
| Winget and Persky ([2022; `COG-06`](https://doi.org/10.5688/ajpe8906)) and Wisniewski, Zierer, and Hattie ([2020; `MOT-05`](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.03087)) | Corrective activity, retest and information-bearing feedback under task and receiver conditions; no universal threshold, feedback type or later-work inference. |
| Carpenter, Pan, and Butler ([2022; `COG-01`](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44159-022-00089-1)), Brunmair and Richter ([2019; `COG-03`](https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000209)), and Czyż, Wójcik, and Solarská ([2024; `COG-04`](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2024.1377122)) | Spacing, retrieval, interleaving and delayed-transfer candidates whose value depends on material, similarity, setting and horizon; no universal gap, mix, repetition count or professional schedule. |
| Kraiger and Ford ([2021; `COG-10`](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-orgpsych-012420-060109)), Matsuo and Tsukube ([2020; `SOC-02`](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijme.2020.100417)), Brooks and colleagues ([2024; `SOC-05`](https://doi.org/10.1002/lrh2.10412)), and Wiese, Kilty, and Bennett ([2018; `SOC-03`](https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.13655)) | Separation of instructional events, learner activity, provider contributions, access, supervision, trust, risk and service pressure; no generic provider credential, capability effect or transplanted clinical governance. |

| Macnamara, Hambrick, and Oswald ([2014; `BEH-02`](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614535810)), Nurse and colleagues ([2024; `BEH-03`](https://doi.org/10.1080/10503307.2024.2308159)), and Sheeran and colleagues ([2020; `MOT-01`](https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000501), [2024; `MOT-03`](https://doi.org/10.1080/10463283.2024.2334563)) | Limits on universal deliberate-practice doses, bounded focused-practice ingredients, target engagement, and conditional if–then planning; no fixed hours threshold, cross-domain causality or professional transfer guarantee. |

HCD.18/.19 use the [material profile's source-informed comparisons](#source-informed-choices-and-limits), with their specific source roles, limits and reopens in the bodies. Their task-based evaluation and ordinal anchors are professional adaptations, not a validated universal score. The M0/M1 walkthrough preserves actual prepared-agent responses; its constructed task facts, material revisions, author-side diagnostic replay and missing target-human observations remain explicit.

The programme and L17 engineering exercise supply designed tasks, stipulated domain facts and constructed observations, not an empirical learner dataset. Real engineering, safety or professional claims require current direct-domain sources and actual case evidence.

`ImpactReview-17-Domain-Oracle-v1` is constructed case data, not a source-ledger entry or currentness claim. Replacing any stipulated engineering correctness or criticality value with a real-world claim requires a named current target-domain Method or result and qualified safety or specialist source.

Refresh only the affected pattern or case claim when a relied-on FPF distinction, direct source contract, target-domain Method or result, specialist boundary, holder, Work family, configuration, evidence window, critical-error predicate, case truth posture, support arrangement, practice condition, or receiving decision changes. A new publication alone does not reopen unaffected claims.

HCD.20–28 use task-sensitive contributions from the official 4C/ID, TBL, Jigsaw and FROG accounts and bounded research on collaboration, visibility and active observation. Their SoTA-Echoing sections state the adopted operation and its limit. HCD.21 adds explicit composition and actual-contact constructions; HCD.24/.25 distinguish comparative judgement from demonstrated transfer; HCD.26 distinguishes prompting from uptake. Juxtapeer, group-formation and contact studies, Edwards and the later CMU feedback study retain their task, population and observation limits. HCD.7 applies tutor-facing assistance through its existing competence, checking and capacity conditions. The linked diagnostic product, numerical resource comparison and recovery variants are authored constructions; they are not empirical outcomes or evidence that one grouping is generally best.

## FPF dependency and compatibility

This edition depends on **First Principles Framework (FPF) — Core Conceptual Specification, Version August 2026**, status **Normative kernel, eternal alpha**, at the current-pattern state qualified for this product, with the bounded C.2.8 dependency below.

FPF supplies System and holder recognition, capability, Method and MethodDescription, Work occurrence and result distinctions, evidence and uncertainty, architecture, agency, decision objects, authority, cultural relations, and precise wording. HCD supplies human-demand, target-or-return, balanced-profile, programme-comparison, development-Method selection, representative-practice, support-arrangement, bounded provider-development, focused-practice, progression, performance-assessment, transfer, retention, evidence-led revision, continuing-development arrangement, bounded HCD Method-repertoire, HCD cultural-continuation guidance, and instructional-material specification and diagnosis for its domain.

`E.23.CDI` governs the independent-System holder condition and later capability-development evidence under its own entry conditions. `E.23.CAE` supplies an observation-first differential where applicability, access, adaptation, enactment, and actual capability change must be separated. `C.32.MWA` prevents source layouts from becoming profile architecture. `C.11.CRC` governs finite comparison inside HCD.2, while `C.11` governs a bounded current-option choice. Compatible FPF changes leave unaffected HCD results reusable; changed relied-on distinctions reopen only their consumers.

For HCD.18, HCD.19 and the instructional-material profile, this edition selects [`C.2.8 U.ExtractableStructuralInformation`](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c28---uextractablestructuralinformation--structure-this-reader-can-recover) from the September 2026 FPF publication of 9 September 2026. It supplies the structural-recovery characteristic of the expressed episteme, its publication form and the reader or observer under specified comparison conditions. Use its own qualitative comparison or structural scale; the profile's material-use values, learning and burden claims keep their own meanings and evidence. Other FPF dependencies retain the basis above. Reopen this bounded dependency when the supplying definition or the receiving structural question changes.

A.19.ECS supplies general evaluation-specification construction to HCD.18. E.22 supplies comparison and E.23 improvement for a material result when those questions are live. General characterization and scale meanings remain with A.17, A.18 and C.16. Material evaluation does not alter the human-evidence or authority boundaries of the other HCD bodies.

## External result and authority boundaries

Target-domain Methods and results govern what counts as correct, safe, critical, or useful in later Work. Clinical, safety, legal, employment, assignment, organization, provider, platform, tool, and specialist owners retain their direct results and authority. HCD may consume those results or return an exact missing value; it does not replace them.

An assisting AI or other System may contribute Work or evidence when its capability, access, configuration, and authority obtain. Its output is not human capability, and it is not the `DecisionSubject` by label. Managers may own allocation and assignment while the human holder participates and while programme, safety, release, clinical, or employment decisions stay separate.

## Edition return

**Human Capability Development Principles Framework — Twenty-nine-pattern edition** designates this shared account and instructional-material profile, its Table of Contents and presentation carrier, and twenty-nine authoritative bodies in reader order: HCD.1, HCD.3, HCD.4, HCD.2, HCD.5, HCD.6, HCD.6.1, HCD.7, HCD.8, HCD.9, HCD.10, HCD.11, HCD.12, HCD.13, HCD.14, HCD.15, HCD.16, HCD.17, HCD.18, HCD.19, HCD.20, HCD.21, HCD.22, HCD.23, HCD.24, HCD.25, HCD.26, HCD.27 and HCD.28. The version date below identifies the edition being used.

The designation identifies the complete HCD pattern set and reader carrier. The Engineering DPF Suite includes this HCD framework alongside its other DPFs and common foundations. Actual use, provider operation, performed development Work, achieved capability, cultural continuation and causal effectiveness require the corresponding observations and decisions described here.

**Description:** HCD is a pattern language for deriving human capability demand from later Work, designing and sustaining development arrangements, judging human contribution, transfer and retention, and evaluating instructional material under stated audience, task, support and time conditions.

**Author:** Anatoly Levenchuk with AI-assisted development and review.

The publication supplies practitioner guidance; evidence for its use in a particular person, provider, programme or population is established at that use.

# Maintenance Engineering and Management Principles Framework Readme

## Practical entries

Maintenance methods connect a condition or failure account with the result someone needs, such as advice, a selected intervention, functioning evidence, return to use or a programme decision. Each connection consumes a particular result. A suitable spare supports readiness; readiness and an operating allowance support a feasible intervention; performed work identifies the configuration to be tested; functioning evidence supports the receiving operating decision.

These are selected examples of the language at work, not a catalogue or a sequence for every request. Enter where the question starts, using adequate existing results. The [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents) provides direct pattern access, and the [Preface](#preface) explains the shared conditions and boundaries. You can ask an assisting agent to explain a pattern or comment on your case in the language of your work, without framework jargon.

The cases are constructed. Their equipment, operating, protection and measurement premises illustrate the reasoning; they do not supply a procedure, time standard or limit for actual equipment. Actual work uses competent practitioners and the applicable professional and operating sources.

### MNT-CARD-01 — From a condition concern to the result actually needed

- **Situation:** A condition concern may justify intervention, but usable support, continuing service and return to operation impose different conditions.
- **Question:** What can be answered now, and what further results does selected physical work actually need?
- **First useful result or blocker:** Sufficient advice, a feasible selected arrangement, or the particular unmet condition limiting the next act.
- **Start with:** [MNT.1 - Identify the Maintained System, Use, and Permission Boundary](#mnt1---identify-the-maintained-system-use-and-permission-boundary) if the unit, use or requested result is unclear; otherwise enter [MNT.6 - Diagnose Condition and Choose a Maintenance Response](#mnt6---diagnose-condition-and-choose-a-maintenance-response) with the adequate condition and failure accounts.
- **Stop or return:** A supported recommendation can finish before repair. Continue only when that intervention is selected and its operative conditions are met; reopen the result whose condition changes.

1. **Give the choice a condition and failure account it can use.** In [PS17](#app-mnt-01--ps17-advice-selected-intervention-and-return-to-use), the question concerns PumpTrain-PS17-B, configuration C41. [MNT.4 - Monitor and Interpret System Condition for Maintenance](#mnt4---monitor-and-interpret-system-condition-for-maintenance) supplies abnormal, increasing bearing-location vibration under comparable duty. [MNT.3 - Establish Degradation and Failure Evidence for Maintenance](#mnt3---establish-degradation-and-failure-evidence-for-maintenance) uses the case's separate machine-specific inspection and diagnostic account: the rolling contact has a localized defect, while the mounting and lubrication findings support replacement under the unchanged design basis.
2. **Finish the bounded recommendation.** The supplied operating assessment permits a lower-duty arrangement that meets present service needs until the planned outage two days away, while its condition and protection limits hold. Normal demand then returns. [MNT.6](#mnt6---diagnose-condition-and-choose-a-maintenance-response) uses that temporary bridge and the identified defect to recommend replacement at the suitable outage. The two days are a service boundary, not a predicted failure time. [MNT.5 - Prepare Maintenance Service Capability, Spares, Tools, and Authority](#mnt5---prepare-maintenance-service-capability-spares-tools-and-authority) finds the spare physically available but its required specialist applicability return missing. The advice is complete; replacement cannot begin. Compatible information, tools and provider preparation can continue.
3. **Test the whole window after the missing support is supplied.** In the extended branch, the applicability return arrives and the intervention is selected. [MNT.7 - Coordinate Maintenance Intervention and Continuing Operation](#mnt7---coordinate-maintenance-intervention-and-continuing-operation) uses a separate operating allowance of four hours for reduced-capacity operation. Thirty minutes for shutdown and isolation, 95 for intervention, 45 for controlled testing, 25 for restoration and hand-back, and thirty of explicit contingency total 225 minutes within 240. Ninety minutes of preparation occurs before the outage. A further twenty-minute demand beyond all included allowances raises the total to 245: revise the arrangement rather than consume required testing or hand-back time.
4. **Carry the selected scope through actual work.** [MNT.8 - Isolate, Make Safe, and Authorize the Maintenance Intervention](#mnt8---isolate-make-safe-and-authorize-the-maintenance-intervention) establishes applicable protection and permission. An uncontrolled shared energy path prevents the affected work from starting. In the branch where the conditions are met, [MNT.9 - Perform and Record the Maintenance Intervention](#mnt9---perform-and-record-the-maintenance-intervention) records removal of bearing R551 and installation of compatible R607, resulting in configuration C42. [MNT.12 - Maintain Maintenance Information and Configuration Continuity](#mnt12---maintain-maintenance-information-and-configuration-continuity) connects the C41 condition history to those events and the C42 test.
5. **Return functioning and control at their supported scope.** [MNT.10 - Verify Restored Functioning after Maintenance](#mnt10---verify-restored-functioning-after-maintenance) uses C42, the applicable acceptance basis and the case's representative run to judge the immediate-duty claim. A failed flow result returns to diagnosis or engineering while the performed intervention remains recorded. With adequate functioning evidence, [MNT.11 - Hand Back and Authorize Resumed Use after Maintenance, with Certification Where Required](#mnt11---hand-back-and-authorize-resumed-use-after-maintenance-with-certification-where-required) reconciles the returned state, obtains any required certification and resumed-use decision, and transfers control. If the receiving authority is unavailable, the test result survives but the intended permission remains outstanding. Return the tested duty and horizon with the permission.

A lost standby train reopens the earlier operating allowance; a finding that a shared mounting defect would defeat replacement reopens [MNT.6](#mnt6---diagnose-condition-and-choose-a-maintenance-response)'s choice. Those changes affect different results. The unchanged evidence remains available, and an unresolved recurrence question need not turn a completed local answer into a new investigation.

### MNT-FLEET — Learn from maintenance history

- **Situation:** One pump group has fewer recorded failures, a proposed monitoring service promises improvement, and an upcoming task already lacks an applicable spare.
- **Question:** Which programme, task or support change does the available evidence warrant?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A comparable fleet account and supported retain or change decision, or the event, exposure or applicability discrepancy that prevents the relevant conclusion.
- **Start with:** [MNT.13 - Coordinate the Maintenance Programme and Fleet Learning](#mnt13---coordinate-the-maintenance-programme-and-fleet-learning), using [MNT.3](#mnt3---establish-degradation-and-failure-evidence-for-maintenance) and [MNT.12](#mnt12---maintain-maintenance-information-and-configuration-continuity) only where the failure or history basis needs work.
- **Stop or return:** Retain an adequate current policy or fix a known support deficiency on its existing basis. Further inquiry is selected only for a worthwhile attainable answer.

1. **Make the comparison mean the same thing.** In the [48-pump case](#app-mnt-02--a-fleet-comparison-that-reverses-when-exposure-is-counted), twenty pumps have four relevant failures over 20,000 operating hours; 28 have six over 56,000 hours. The crude rates are 0.20 and approximately 0.107 events per 1,000 hours. Counts favor the first group, rates the second. [MNT.3](#mnt3---establish-degradation-and-failure-evidence-for-maintenance) establishes what counts as a failure, and [MNT.12](#mnt12---maintain-maintenance-information-and-configuration-continuity) attaches events and exposure to the actual components and intervals.
2. **Propagate a corrected history before changing the policy.** If two of the second group's six records are preventive removals, correct that event classification and the affected rate. Duty, component histories and selection into the groups still limit any causal policy comparison.
3. **Keep a policy decision separate from a support decision.** [MNT.2 - Select and Reopen the Maintenance Policy](#mnt2---select-and-reopen-the-maintenance-policy) can retain the current task where its existing failure-and-response basis remains adequate. The weak comparative data do not establish that adequacy. [MNT.13](#mnt13---coordinate-the-maintenance-programme-and-fleet-learning) can separately select repair of the known spare deficiency, using [MNT.5](#mnt5---prepare-maintenance-service-capability-spares-tools-and-authority) to establish readiness for the upcoming task. A broader redesign of recurring support returns to the relevant enabling-arrangement practice; it need not wait for a causal fleet study.
4. **Compare the proposed method at the response it can improve.** [MNT.14 - Compare Maintenance Methods for Retention or Change](#mnt14---compare-maintenance-methods-for-retention-or-change) compares the online predictor with current periodic interpretation at the same maintenance use. In its case, existing provider information shows no improvement in feasible response: the same specialist and part constraints dominate, while integration and interpretation add work. Retain the present method for that use and address support. Another family with rapidly changing condition and an available response can reopen the comparison for that family.

The policy alternatives also depend on the function. An obvious, low-consequence indicator failure may justify deliberate run-to-failure; a hidden protective-function failure needs an applicable means of finding it.

### MNT-SHARED-WORK — Reconcile individually feasible jobs that cannot be performed together

- **Situation:** Two maintenance jobs fit their own windows but demand the same specialist or fallback.
- **Question:** Which combined commitment can actually be met, and what does changing it do to service and failure consequences?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A supported allocation or timing change, or the specific combined commitment that remains infeasible.
- **Start with:** [MNT.15 - Reconcile Simultaneous Maintenance, Operation, and Support Work](#mnt15---reconcile-simultaneous-maintenance-operation-and-support-work), using the existing job, readiness and operating accounts.
- **Stop or return:** A simple shared-demand bound can finish the feasibility question. Selecting a repair needs the relevant consequence, capability and authority results.

1. **Compare the whole shared demand.** In the [packaging-plant case](#app-mnt-03--individually-feasible-jobs-and-one-shared-specialist), each job needs four hours of the same qualified specialist inside one six-hour access window. Eight hours cannot fit six. Preparation overlapping production leaves the shared eight-hour specialist demand unchanged.
2. **Use the separate methods to distinguish feasible alternatives.** [MNT.6](#mnt6---diagnose-condition-and-choose-a-maintenance-response) supplies the failure consequence of deferring a job; [MNT.5](#mnt5---prepare-maintenance-service-capability-spares-tools-and-authority) determines whether an additional provider is capable, available and permitted to act; [MNT.7](#mnt7---coordinate-maintenance-intervention-and-continuing-operation) checks another window or changed operating arrangement against continuing service. [MNT.15](#mnt15---reconcile-simultaneous-maintenance-operation-and-support-work) consumes those results to return a supported combined arrangement or an unmet commitment.
3. **Reopen the combination when a shared premise changes.** If both jobs rely on the same standby equipment, each plan's separate fallback claim no longer settles their joint use. Extend the comparison to the actual operating dependencies and relevant [MNT.8](#mnt8---isolate-make-safe-and-authorize-the-maintenance-intervention) protection conditions. If a longer shift would impair the specialist's later protected work, change allocation, relief or timing.

## How to read and apply the framework

Use a pattern's Problem frame and Solution for the first working move. Its worked case shows the result and a consequential branch. Its checklist, source comparison and relations provide the further assurance and context needed for a more consequential use.

## Citation

Cite: Anatoly Levenchuk, *Maintenance Engineering and Management Principles Framework*, version shown above. For a particular contribution, add its PatternID and title. The framework was developed with AI-assisted authoring and review. The original text is reusable under the license above; cited third-party works are not relicensed by this publication.

# Preface

## MNT.Preface:1 - The working problem and practical gain

A useful maintenance result connects knowledge of a System's condition to the functioning that someone needs. The practitioner may be an engineer choosing policy, a technician preparing an intervention, a planner coordinating access, an operator receiving control or a programme lead comparing fleet history. Their questions are related, but their results differ.

The name makes both engineering and management visible. Engineering includes failure interpretation, intervention choice and functioning verification. Management includes policy, service capability, information, programme, coordination and continuation of actual practice, not just scheduling or resource administration. Maintenance Engineering and Maintenance Management are both established expressions; the shorter engineering name also has broad uses. This framework's compound name makes its connected contribution explicit without dividing the sixteen Methods into two separate products.

An abnormal signal alone does not decide the response. The relevant failure may be uncertain, a suitable part may be unavailable, or testing and restoration may not fit the loss-of-service window. At fleet scale, raw counts can favour the wrong group. At practice scale, a revised manual can be available while the older Method remains in use.

The language helps readers make those connections without imposing a complete intervention-and-return sequence on every request. Its gain is a supported maintenance decision, feasible selected work and a truthful account of what can be used afterwards. A recommendation or a decision to retain an adequate policy can be that complete result. A stronger claim is withheld only by the limit that actually affects it.

The maintained subject is the functioning of Systems in use, especially physical and cyber-physical equipment under identifiable operating conditions. Maintenance includes preserving or restoring the required contribution and selecting its policies, support and programme. It interacts with engineering design, operation, organizational provision and asset management. A choice about an asset's continued use, renewal, replacement, repurposing or withdrawal retains its own value-oriented decision, as do a new service concept and a changed engineered design.

For one pump, selecting maintenance policy or an intervention to preserve or restore required functioning is a maintenance result. Comparing whether to continue its use or choose another asset option by value, costs, risks and service effects is an asset-management result, even for that single pump. Conversely, coordinating a fleet's maintenance programme remains MNT.13. A replacement may occur in either question; the verb, horizon, job title and number of assets do not decide the boundary. One case can need both contributions.

The adjacent Engineering Asset Management Principles Framework concerns engineered assets, asset Systems and portfolios. Related [Enterprise Asset Management](https://www.sap.com/resources/what-is-eam) terminology also includes substantial physical-asset, maintenance, information and cross-functional practice; it does not mean software alone. The two field expressions do not make every external source's scope identical. A particular receiving question identifies which asset-management contribution is needed. Asset existence and use over time are distinct from how engineering Work is organized; no universal sequence of engineering stages follows.

## MNT.Preface:2 - Organizing the Methods around different results

The sixteen patterns are grouped into four publication Parts:

- Part A identifies the maintained use, chooses policy and interprets failure and condition through [MNT.1](#mnt1---identify-the-maintained-system-use-and-permission-boundary)–MNT.4.
- Part B makes a present response feasible and properly bounded through [MNT.5](#mnt5---prepare-maintenance-service-capability-spares-tools-and-authority)–MNT.8.
- Part C distinguishes performed intervention, restored functioning and return to use through [MNT.9](#mnt9---perform-and-record-the-maintenance-intervention)–MNT.11.
- Part D maintains information, programme learning, Method choice, simultaneous coordination and cultural continuation through [MNT.12](#mnt12---maintain-maintenance-information-and-configuration-continuity)–MNT.16.

These are navigation groups. They do not assert four stages of every job or one composite Method containing all sixteen contributions. Enter a Method where the question starts, using current adequate evidence or a qualified equivalent result. An unused sibling contributes no prerequisite.

A typical condition-to-intervention route starts with an interpreted condition from [MNT.4](#mnt4---monitor-and-interpret-system-condition-for-maintenance) and a choice from MNT.6. Readiness from [MNT.5](#mnt5---prepare-maintenance-service-capability-spares-tools-and-authority) and operating coordination from [MNT.7](#mnt7---coordinate-maintenance-intervention-and-continuing-operation) qualify feasible performance. [MNT.8](#mnt8---isolate-make-safe-and-authorize-the-maintenance-intervention) establishes the protection and permission for the selected act. [MNT.9](#mnt9---perform-and-record-the-maintenance-intervention) then supplies evidence of work and actual configuration; [MNT.10](#mnt10---verify-restored-functioning-after-maintenance) supplies the functioning result; [MNT.11](#mnt11---hand-back-and-authorize-resumed-use-after-maintenance-with-certification-where-required) supplies hand-back and resumed-use permission. The route is conditional: it stops earlier when the requested result is already adequate.

Other questions use different connections. [MNT.12](#mnt12---maintain-maintenance-information-and-configuration-continuity)'s maintenance history supports [MNT.13](#mnt13---coordinate-the-maintenance-programme-and-fleet-learning) only where events and exposure are comparable. [MNT.14](#mnt14---compare-maintenance-methods-for-retention-or-change) compares a Method's practical worth; [MNT.16](#mnt16---deliberately-continue-and-change-maintenance-culture) examines whether variants are transmitted and enacted in the practice population. [MNT.15](#mnt15---reconcile-simultaneous-maintenance-operation-and-support-work) handles common conditions that separate successful job decisions cannot establish.

**Constituent actions in ongoing work.** During a repair, a diagnostic observation may constitute part of locating the fault, and fault location may be part of restoring the equipment's required functioning. The relevant skills lie at several grains: handling the instrument, interpreting the reading under the operating conditions and coordinating the intervention with the maintained service. If the service must remain available through standby equipment, a diagnostic action that would disable that standby changes the whole arrangement. [MNT.15](#mnt15---reconcile-simultaneous-maintenance-operation-and-support-work) compares the affected commitments; B.1.5.EW helps expose the connection. Completed diagnosis leaves the repair, functioning and hand-back questions with their own Methods.

## MNT.Preface:3 - What the principal objects mean in practice

A maintained System is the equipment or other System whose contribution is at issue. A part is an actual constituent; a part number can describe many such individuals. A configuration is the relevant actual arrangement and values over an interval; a configuration description carries claims about it.

An observation says what was measured or inspected. A diagnosis explains the condition to the degree supported. A prognosis concerns future condition under stated assumptions. The maintenance choice uses these accounts but also considers feasible response and consequence.

A policy is the reusable selection of task and applicability conditions. A particular intervention decision selects a response now. A Method is a reusable way of obtaining a result; this framework's pattern prose explains those ways. A plan describes intended work, while the performed work and its effects require evidence of what occurred.

These distinctions matter where they change action. Ordinary equipment and maintenance language is enough elsewhere; a routine repair need not acquire an ontology form. FPF supplies the general recognition, evidence, comparison, permission and assurance Methods. MNT adds the failure, task, support, operating and restoration reasoning that those general contributions do not decide by themselves.

## MNT.Preface:4 - Competing values and the whole-use constraints

Maintenance balances failure consequences with intervention burden and disturbance. Earlier detection is useful only if its interpretation and response can improve the result. More stock, inspection or data can help, but also consume resources or displace more valuable work. A programme decision includes whose downtime, effort and exposure are counted.

Two whole-use constraints are especially visible in the applications. [MNT.7](#mnt7---coordinate-maintenance-intervention-and-continuing-operation)'s PS17 calculation accounts for the complete outage, including controlled testing, restoration and contingency. [MNT.15](#mnt15---reconcile-simultaneous-maintenance-operation-and-support-work)'s shared-specialist example compares the combined demand, not just each job's separate fit. Those sections carry the respective calculations; affected decisions return there instead of treating local approvals as proof of the whole combination.

Where a protective or administrative requirement is disputed, assess its merits as well as preserving its present force. Identify the protected party, relevant harm and evidence, the baseline and incremental protection, the full burden and displaced harms, and who can amend it. Harmful retention or tightening deserves the same scrutiny as harmful relaxation. The existence of a rule does not prove its proportionality; disagreement with it does not cancel its authority.

## MNT.Preface:5 - Architectural Rationale

The language follows recurring differences in maintenance decisions. Policy is reusable across cases; diagnosis and intervention choice concern the present case. Support and operation can defeat a technically plausible repair. Protection governs a selected act. Intervention, functioning and permission produce different claims. History, fleet learning and practice continuation work across longer horizons and populations.

Collapsing these questions into “maintain the asset” would shorten the index but leave the practitioner to invent their connections. Turning them into one mandatory workflow would create a different failure: a sufficient recommendation would wait for part certification, an outage and release that the advice request never asked to perform. The conditional arrangement retains professional depth and useful early completion together.

A technology ladder from reactive through predictive to autonomous is also insufficient.
